turns.text: hey need a linkedin banner image + a simple funnel graphic of my application pipeline. making a visual at midnight, normal behavior
Happy to. For the banner: what's your field or target role, and any text you want on it (name, headline, tagline)? For the funnel: what numbers should it show, and what stages do you track?

target is summer 2026 supply chain / transportation analyst intern, bay area. banner should match my v-whatever resume styling, clean, one page energy, nothing flashy

funnel starts at 40 active targets. i just cut th spreadsheet down from way more. ngl volume isn't working for me like it does for everyone else lol. want th funnel to look deliberate not like i gave up

Framing it as a focused pipeline works well. I don't know your resume's fonts or colors, so I'll go with a neutral navy, white and light gray look with a clean sans-serif, which is a safe match for most one-page resumes. Tell me your actual colors and I'll adjust.

Here's what I made:

[Image: LinkedIn banner, 1584x396. Off-white background with a thin navy rule along the bottom. Left side in bold navy sans-serif: "Logistics Management | Supply Chain & Transportation Analytics". Beneath it in smaller gray text: "Seeking Summer 2026 Analyst Internship, Bay Area". Right side has a minimal line-art icon of a route network with three connected nodes. Lots of white space.]

[Image: Funnel graphic, horizontal, four tapering bars in descending shades of navy. Top bar: "40 Active Targets, researched and prioritized". Next: "Tailored Applications". Next: "Conversations & Screens". Final bar: "Offers". Title above: "A Focused Pipeline: Quality Over Volume". The lower stages have blank number fields for you to fill in.]

The "researched and prioritized" label makes the 40 read as a choice. Want a tagline on the banner too?
love it. also my tuesday 3pm mock interview with lena went fine today, but i sounded way less sure than i want to look on paper. can th visual look more confident than i sounded

Sure. Visuals can carry confidence without overclaiming. I'd make these changes:

[Image: Updated banner. The headline is larger and bolder, with a short confident tagline: "Turning supply chain data into decisions." The navy is a bit deeper, and a thin accent line sits under the headline.]

[Image: Updated funnel. The top bar is wider and bolder with "40 Targets, Hand-Selected". Active verbs on each stage: "Tailor", "Engage", "Convert". Title: "Targeted Pipeline".]

The wording is direct and specific, so it reads assured. Want me to swap the tagline for something else?
Done. Both are ready for the final version once you pick your exact colors. Good luck with the applications.
